title: The Fawn and His Mother

full_text:
A young fawn was browsing in a peaceful forest clearing with his mother. Looking admiringly at his mother's graceful, slender limbs, sharp hooves, and keen ears, the young buck asked:

"Mother, why are you always so terrified of the dogs? You are much larger and swifter than they are; your hooves can deliver a crushing blow; you have sharp senses that detect danger miles away, and when I grow my antlers, we could easily pierce any hound. Why do you always flee at the first sound of their bark?"

The mother hind smiled tenderly and stroked her son's head:

"Every word you speak is the absolute truth, my child. I tell myself the very same things every single day: that I am swift, that I am large, and that I should stand my ground. But alas! The moment I hear the distant baying of a single hound echoing across the hills, all my courage evaporates in an instant, and my legs carry me away before I even know I am running!"
moral: No amount of logical reasoning can cure a heart ruled by inherited fear.
